module_title: Work-Energy Theorem, Collisions, and Energy Transformations
introduction: This level covers advanced mechanics concepts often tested in NDA and CDS, including how energy transforms in real-world devices and the physics of crashes (collisions).

core_concepts.title: Work-Energy Theorem
core_concepts.description:
This theorem states that the 'Net Work done' by all forces acting on a body equals the 'Change in its Kinetic Energy'. 
Formula: $W_{net} = KE_{final} - KE_{initial}$. 
Application: This is used to calculate the stopping distance of a car when brakes are applied.

core_concepts.title: Elastic vs. Inelastic Collisions
core_concepts.description:
1. Elastic Collision: Both Momentum and Kinetic Energy are conserved. (e.g., ideal billiard balls hitting each other). 
2. Inelastic Collision: Only Momentum is conserved, but Kinetic Energy is LOST (usually as heat or sound). (e.g., a car crash, a bullet getting embedded in a wooden block).

core_concepts.title: Energy Transformation Devices
core_concepts.description:
The transformation of energy from one form to another is a favorite static GK topic: 
- Dynamo/Generator: Mechanical $\rightarrow$ Electrical. 
- Electric Motor: Electrical $\rightarrow$ Mechanical. 
- Microphone: Sound $\rightarrow$ Electrical. 
- Loudspeaker: Electrical $\rightarrow$ Sound. 
- Solar Cell: Light $\rightarrow$ Electrical. 
- Battery (Discharging): Chemical $\rightarrow$ Electrical.

important_entities.name: Escape Velocity & Energy
important_entities.significance: To escape Earth's gravity, an object must be given enough Kinetic Energy to overcome its negative Gravitational Potential Energy. When it reaches infinity, its total energy becomes exactly zero.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In ANY type of collision (elastic or perfectly inelastic), Linear Momentum is always conserved. Only Kinetic Energy is lost in inelastic collisions. Never say momentum is lost in a car crash.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Mic takes your Voice (Sound -> Electricity). Speaker gives it back (Electricity -> Sound).
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Do not confuse the two. A microphone generates an electrical signal from your voice.

exam_strategy_tips: State PCS exams frequently ask you to match the 'Device' with its 'Energy Transformation'. Memorize the list of transformation devices thoroughly.
